intro: The Carpathian Mountains curve through Romania like a giant arc, wrapping around Transylvania, and the Danube ends its long journey in a vast delta on the Black Sea.

chapters.title: Carpathians and Transylvania
text: The Carpathians form a great arc through the middle of the country; Moldoveanu is the highest peak, and the Transfăgărășan road twists dramatically over the mountains. Inside the arc is the plateau of Transylvania, with fortified villages and castles.
Romania borders Ukraine, Moldova, Bulgaria, Serbia and Hungary, and has a coast on the Black Sea.

chapters.title: Delta and wildlife
text: The Danube Delta is one of Europe's largest and best-preserved wetlands, home to pelicans and hundreds of other bird species. Romania's forests shelter more brown bears than any other European country outside Russia, along with wolves and lynx.

keyTerms.meaning: Flat wetland where a river splits into channels before reaching the sea.
